title: Motorcycle-graph T-mesh (Eppstein 2008 / Campen 2015 / Lyon 2021)
description:
**Depends on PATCH-40.** Stage 3 of the QGP pipeline: build a T-mesh on the surface by tracing iso-lines of the seamless parametrization. Implements the motorcycle graph from Eppstein-Goodrich-Kim-Tamstorf 2008, with the Lyon 2021 modification where motorcycles can survive crashes (regular valence-4 nodes form at intersections).

**Algorithm (Lyon 2021 modified motorcycle graph):**
1. Each singularity emits motorcycle traces along all 4 cardinal directions of its parametrization (±u, ±v).
2. Each trace follows iso-lines of the parametrization through the mesh.
3. When traces intersect: in the original motorcycle graph trace stops; in Lyon's modification it can continue (regular valence-4 node forms).
4. Stopping criterion (Lyon 2021 Sec 3): a trace stops once it has intersected two traces tk and tl such that αik ∈ [0, α] and αil ∈ [-α, 0] — i.e., on both sides of trace ti a trace is found such that the formed triangle is contained in the sector of half-angle α around ti. α is the user-given angular bound (default 5° to 35°).
5. Build T-mesh structure: nodes (singularities + intersections), arcs (trace segments between consecutive nodes), patches (rectangular regions bounded by 4 arcs in the parametric domain).

**Output:** T-mesh data structure (nodes N, arcs A, patches P) ready for quantization.

References:
- Algorithm spec: Ixdar/ixdar-tickets/PATCH-37-CAMPEN-SPEC.md (Stage 2 section, plus Lyon 2021 modification noted in PATCH-37 description)
- metriko reference: /tmp/metriko/include/metriko/core/tmesh/ (~604 LOC C++)
- Eppstein-Goodrich-Kim-Tamstorf 2008. Motorcycle Graphs: Canonical Quad Mesh Partitioning. CGF 27(5).
- Campen-Bommes-Kobbelt 2015. Quantized Global Parametrization. SIGGRAPH Asia.
- Lyon-Campen-Kobbelt 2021. Quad Layouts via Constrained T-Mesh Quantization. CGF 40(2). Sec 3.
definition-of-done: 1. MotorcycleGraph + TMesh classes produce nodes, arcs, patches from a seamless parametrization. 2. Cube parametrization yields 6 patches (one per face), 8 nodes (corners). 3. Sphere with 8 ±1/4 singularities yields the topologically-expected T-mesh. 4. Hand.obj matches metriko's T-mesh node/arc/patch counts at α=10° and α=30°.
testing-plan: 1. Cube parametrization (analytic): expect exactly 6 patches, 12 arcs, 8 nodes. 2. Torus seamless parametrization (analytic): expect 1 patch, 2 arcs, 1 node. 3. Hand.obj at α=10°/15°/30°: counts within 5% of metriko.
